seoDescription: Learn to create a stunning Medusa look inspired by Greek mythology with this detailed SFX tutorial. This guide walks you through crafting an intricate snake headpiece from simple materials like wooden sticks, a wig base, foam, and toy snakes, finishing it with golden paint. You'll also master the special effects makeup, including how to make and apply your own custom liquid latex prosthetics for a seamless, serpentine effect. The tutorial covers key techniques like hiding eyebrows, dramatic contouring, painting scales, and adding black tears.

summary:
## Medusa Headpiece Construction

- **Frame**: The base is a simple **headband**. Lightweight, hollowed **wooden sticks** are hot-glued onto it to create a crown-like structure, which is then spray-painted **gold**.
- **Snake Hair**: A cheap wig is used for its **wig cap** base after the hair is cut off. Strips of **black foam sheets** are glued on, then curled with heat to create a texture of moving snakes. The entire piece is spray-painted black.
- **Assembly**: Realistic **toy snakes** and the golden stick frame are glued securely onto the foam-covered wig cap. Use your imagination to add other **gold decorations** for extra detail.

## Custom SFX Prosthetics

- **Material**: The prosthetics are made from a simple **liquid latex paste**, created by mixing **liquid latex** with **baking flour**.
- **Process**: The paste is smeared onto a **face-shaped form** (like a mannequin head). Pieces of **toy snakes** (like tails) are embedded into the paste. The piece is then briefly microwaved for a few seconds to cure and solidify the latex.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> When peeling the finished prosthetic off its form, apply generous amounts of **powder** or flour to the surface. This prevents the latex from sticking to itself and tearing.

## Makeup Application

- **Brow Hiding**: A three-step process to create a smooth canvas:
  1. Use a **glue stick** to flatten the eyebrow hairs.
  2. Apply an **orange concealer** to neutralize the dark color of the brows.
  3. Cover with a layer of skin-toned **foundation**.

- **Prosthetic Application**: Use a skin-safe adhesive like **Pros-Aide** to attach the forehead and cheek prosthetics. Blend the edges seamlessly into the skin using more adhesive.

- **Base & Contouring**:
  - After setting the prosthetics with powder, apply **foundation** over the entire face.
  - Use **rusty and black eyeshadows** for heavy contouring to create a gaunt, serpentine look. Focus on defining the nose to make it appear more snake-like.
  - Use **black hairspray** on the outer edges of the face and neck for soft, faded shading.

- **Detailing**:
  - **Scales**: Paint scale patterns on the cheeks and forehead. A mesh fabric can be used as a stencil.
  - **Gold Accents**: Add small dabs of **gold paint** to the scales to visually connect the face makeup with the golden headpiece.
  - **Eyes**: Create a dramatic, earthy **smoky eye** using brown and black shades. Deepen the waterline with a black pencil, add a sharp **eyeliner** wing, and apply **false lashes**.
  - **Black Tears**: For a final dramatic touch, use heavily watered-down **black watercolor paint** and let it drip down the cheeks to create realistic tears.
  - **Lips**: Define the lips with a dark lip pencil to complete the look.

## Planning and Materials Overview

In this tutorial we are diving into Greek mythology, so be careful. A look like this requires beginner to intermediate skills, takes forever to prepare, and about one hour to apply. ## Constructing the Golden Headpiece Frame

So, let's start out with that headpiece. We have like, these are like, we did kind of hollow it out a little, wooden sticks thingy. So you can use whatever you have. These were kind of lightweight and yeah, stick them to a headband. You can choose to build this on a head like we do, but of course, you can also build it up laying down on the table. A little glue strip there to keep them together at the base, and then we glue more of these onto the headband. Then we go in and do a little trimming, make them look just the way we want. And this is where you can get creative and shape this headpiece any way you like it. There is no real right or wrong here, so just go ahead and do your thing.

And Ellie kind of missed the opportunity when she spoke about the look here in the intro. She had the chance to make one of the best dad jokes ever, but that was not on the menu. Anyways, keep on building that headpiece. See, Ellie has to spread those sticks apart, make them in little groups. I'm putting sticks on top of my head, and in Swedish that's just 'pinnar på mitt huvud'.

## Creating the Snake Hair Wig Base

Done and done. Time for a little golden spray. I almost said gilding our... oh my god, I must be tired. Anyways, the gold spray there to get the shine on. 

And then we take a nasty old wig and simply cut all the hair off because we need that support from that base of the wig so that we can keep a headpiece in place, 'cause it's gonna be huge. Black paint on that. And then we take these foam sheet pieces, cut them out in strips, and simply glue them straight on, creating that snaky-like hair. This process actually takes a while. And then this whole look, we've been working on for quite a while. We did a little this week, a little next week, and yeah, so that's why it took so long to create. 

But anyway, a little black spray there, and we are good to go. And what we're doing now is simply to curl these up, make them little snake-like in the shape. And this is, you know, there is again no right or wrong here. Just twirly, snaky looking shapes back there. And yeah. More of that water-based spray paint, get that black color on. And then we bring in those little tiny toy snakes that Ellie found in the store.

## Assembling the Full Medusa Headpiece

Yeah, glue them on there. Get the real snake vibe going. Next up, gluing that golden headpiece straight on there as well, so we get everything in one solid unit. More snakes and decorations. These golden things are just stuff we found around the house. It can be pretty much anything, so use your imagination. Use whatever you feel would be cool here. 

And since we are on the topic of Medusa here, if you could turn one thing in the world into stone, what would that be? Would it be a person or would it be a flying pig or what would you turn into stone if you could? Tell us in the comments.

## Crafting the Liquid Latex Prosthetics

Alright, next up, a nice little prosthetic-y going from our forehead up and to the back of these. So using liquid latex paste, basically liquid latex mixed with baking flour into a paste, and smear that out onto anything face-shaped that can be a match to your forehead. Basically doesn't have to be super exact. We'll need a piece there up on the forehead going down a bit and into this we're gonna sink those additional snakes. Snake tail, push that in, and additional latex there over, actually. Yeah. And again, add as many as you like. And you don't even want them there, but it looks cool. Kind of makes the face go into snakes. So yeah, we thought it'd look pretty awesome. So there you go. We also create these for the cheekbones. So after we run this in the micro a few seconds to make it solid, go for the cheekbones. There we go. Do the same thing right there.

## Detailing and Prepping the Pieces

Now going back to our headpiece for additional detailing. This time, it's gold paint on those scales of the snakes. Need them to pop a little bit more to match the headpiece in general. So yeah, and with the gold paint, just tiny light strokes there to highlight some of those scales. And of course, the same thing right there on the prosthetic. Put that shine on those snakes. 

And then it's time to peel that forehead prosthetic off. And be sure to apply ample amounts of powder or flour as you peel it off, or that latex will simply stick to itself. 

Now, let's check out Rygel SFX. I have met this awesome dude, and I think you should check out these super cool creations and give this guy a follow. He deserves it.

## Applying the Headpiece and Hiding Brows

The application, of course, requires us to... I shouldn't say remove, but at least get rid of temporarily, all that hair. So tuck it in, tuck it away, and bring out your awesome headpiece and put that straight on there. Yeah, right about there. Looking good. Maybe adjust it a bit. 

And then it's time for a three-stage brow hiding process, beginning with a bit of glue stick there, flatten those brows, and go in with an orange concealer to cancel out the colors of those brows. And on top of that, we go in with a foundation. The clip with a concealer application was lost, so we went straight to that foundation clip here in the tutorial. But yeah, use all three. 

And then we head on to merge that headpiece into our little forehead with a little black faded line there using a black hair spray color. 

And head on to apply Pros-Aide to attach our prosthetic. And this, of course, will work with any kind of skin adhesive that you have access to. All right, so put it on there. Go over the edges there with additional Pros-Aide, and then head on to the cheekbones.

## Applying Prosthetics and Contouring

Setting the whole thing with powder and then going back to foundation. For the shading we are going with a rusty kind of tone. Well good, we're going to mix that in with additional black later on. And these black tones will help us to fade that prosthetic into the headpiece and also give all that shading that extra punch and define the nose a little bit better to enhance the snake theme.

## Painting Scales and Adding Final Shading

We go in and add a little scales on various patches on the face. And for the curious ones in the audience, if you are wondering what this voice-over guy actually is doing when he's not doing voice-overs for Ellimacs SFX, you can check that out at Macs Moser on Instagram. Go check it out.

And for the outermost sides in cheek and neck, we actually go in with that black hair spray paint, fade some of that black into the face. Then we're gonna switch to gold again to connect our face a little bit more to the actual headpiece by adding randomly placed little gold spots there in those scales.

## Dramatic Eye Makeup and Finishing Details

Closing in on the finish line, but we still need to pack a little more punch there, especially around the eyes. They look a little bit nude at the moment. So, yeah, going in with brown earthy tones here for a nice smoky look. And again, bringing in that black to increase that punch and impact. 

I'm starting to see the finish line, in Swedish: 'jag börjar se mållinjen'. But we are not on that finish line just yet. We need additional eyeliner here, and we also need to deepen and darken that waterline. So for an extravagant look like this, we cannot forget the brows, so draw them in there. Those falsies. And when they are in place, time to go into selfie mode and story mode, like 6,000 angles here. 

Anywho, tears. Tears are good, especially if they are black. So, basic watercolor with a lot of water makes it run down your cheek. Look at that. Perfect.

## Final Touches and Reveal

And finally, we go in and define those lips a little bit better with a pen. And then we call it a day. You can, of course, add additional stuff to this, but all in all, you are one hell of an awesome Medusa, don't you think so? We think this look came out super cool.
